source: CPTS Module 03: Network Enumeration with Nmap

examples.label: Connect via netcat from source port 53

references.title: HTB Academy - Network Enumeration with Nmap

name: Evasion - Trusted Source Port (53)
description: Firewalls often trust traffic from port 53 (DNS). Scanning from --source-port 53 can slip past a filtered port; netcat can then connect from the same source port.

defense.why_it_works: Some firewalls and IDS/IPS systems are configured to trust traffic from TCP port 53 (DNS). Using --source-port 53 exploits this trust rule, causing packets to be passed through firewall rules that would otherwise block them.
defense.prerequisites: Network access and a firewall that trusts a specific source port (e.g. 53/DNS).
defense.impact: Bypass of source-port-based ACLs, reaching ports that would otherwise be filtered.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1046 AN1583] Monitor for execution of network enumeration utilities (nmap, netcat, net.exe, ping.exe, tracert.exe) in short succession, particularly when chained with lateral movement tools or system enumeration commands. [AN1584] Sequential ping, arp, or traceroute commands issued from bash scripts or interactive shells to map remote hosts are a strong behavioral indicator.
defense.artifacts: Traffic sourced from port 53 (or another trusted port) toward unusual destination ports in firewall logs.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=network
| stats dc(dest_port) as ports dc(dest_ip) as hosts by src_ip, bin(_time, 1m)
| where ports>15 OR hosts>25

index=suricata event_type=alert alert.signature="*scan*"
| table _time, src_ip, dest_ip
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| summarize ports=dcount(RemotePort), hosts=dcount(RemoteIP), conns=count() by LocalIP, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where ports > 15 or hosts > 25
| sort by ports desc
// nmap --source-port scan (spoofs a trusted source port like 53/88)
defense.sigma_rules: net_port_scan_activity (nmap --source-port scan (spoofs a trusted source port like 53/88))
defense.prevention:
Do not create firewall allow rules based on source port alone. Configure IDS/IPS to properly inspect all traffic including packets sourced from port 53.

[MITRE T1046 M1042] Disable or remove unnecessary services and functionality that expose attack surface. [M1030] Implement network segmentation to limit the set of hosts reachable from any given compromised system. Use firewalls to restrict which source addresses can reach each service port.
defense.evasion: Setting a trusted source port (--source-port 53/80/443) defeats firewalls that allow traffic from DNS/HTTP/HTTPS by port; pair with slow timing and fragmentation for stealthier probing.
defense.misconfiguration: Network perimeters that do not filter ICMP, do not use egress filtering, or expose unnecessary services (all ports open) allow comprehensive port scanning. Systems without host-based firewalls or IDS/IPS allow scan traffic to enumerate every open service, revealing attack surface. No rate-limiting on inbound probes means stealth scans complete quickly.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# No firewall between attacker and target (or overly permissive rules):
# iptables -L  ->  Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)  [no rules]
# Or: Windows Firewall disabled
# Every service's port is reachable from any source

# No IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata not deployed; no AWS GuardDuty / Azure Defender
# Nmap SYN scan completes in seconds with no alert generated
defense.secure_config:
# Linux host-based firewall - default-deny inbound:
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
# Only open required services:
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT  # HTTPS only
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -s 10.10.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT  # SSH from mgmt network

# Rate-limit scan detection (drops SYN floods):
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -m limit --limit 1/s --limit-burst 3 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -j DROP

# Deploy IDS/IPS:
# Snort/Suricata rules detect nmap OS detection probes
# AWS: GuardDuty (detects port scans from EC2)
# Cloud: Security Groups default-deny with explicit allow rules

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, NetFlow / sFlow, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Check for unusual network connections to/from the source host
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Scans from a trusted source port to slip past a firewall:
  -p50000 -sS   SYN-scan the target port
  -Pn -n --disable-arp-ping --packet-trace   no discovery/DNS/ARP, show packets
  --source-port 53   send from port 53 (DNS), which many firewalls implicitly trust
If a port looked filtered normally but responds from source-port 53, the firewall trusts DNS traffic; connect through with 'ncat --source-port 53'.
